title: Palindrome After At Most One Deletion
statement: You are given a string s made up only of lowercase English letters. Return True if s is already a palindrome, OR if it can be turned into a palindrome by deleting at most one character; otherwise return False. Deleting zero characters is allowed, so any string that is already a palindrome returns True. The empty string and any single-character string are palindromes and return True. Walk two pointers inward from the two ends: as long as the characters match, keep going. At the first mismatch you are permitted exactly one deletion, which means you must check BOTH possibilities and return True if EITHER works: skipping the left character (comparing the segment one position right of left through right) leaves a palindrome, OR skipping the right character (comparing left through one position left of right) leaves a palindrome. If neither branch yields a palindrome, return False. Return a boolean (True or False).
hints: When you compare characters from both ends of the string, what should you do the moment the two ends disagree, given you get one free deletion?
March two pointers inward while ends match. At the first mismatch you have one deletion to spend, and it could go to either side, so you must test both skip-left and skip-right, not just one.

Write a helper is_pal(lo, hi) that checks whether s[lo..hi] is a plain palindrome. Advance left/right while s[left] == s[right]. On the first mismatch, return is_pal(left+1, right) OR is_pal(left, right-1). If the loop finishes with no mismatch, the string was already a palindrome, so return True.
